close_reason:
Landed in commit 127eaf0 (testjig SSE Last-Event-ID + WS pushState replay), paired with cf7p.10 per Mark's 2026-05-13 acceptance ('option (2) pair with cf7p.10 in one PR sharing the same event-id scheme'). Same producer-driven event log in crate-jmap-testjig/src/replay.rs.

Acceptance criteria status:

- 'Outbound StateChange frames include a pushState field per RFC 8887 §4.3.5.1': YES. build_state_change_frame() now emits {'@type':'StateChange', 'changed':{...}, 'pushState':'<u64>'} where pushState is the decimal encoding of the largest event id in the emitted batch.

- 'The pushState encodes enough server state that on PushEnable with a prior pushState, the server can emit all StateChange events that have happened since': YES. parse_push_state() parses the u64; handle_push_enable() threads it into push_loop() which uses it as the initial last_seen. If the value is within the log's retained window, emit_pending() replays past entries on the first wake.

- 'New tests/ws_resume.rs integration test exercises reconnect-with-pushState replay': YES. tests/ws_resume.rs::push_state_replays_missed_changes asserts the full cycle: open WS+PushEnable, mutate, capture pushState from frame, close WS, mutate twice with no WS, reopen WS with WebSocketPushEnable.pushState=captured, observe replay frame with pushState > captured.

- 'Design likely couples to JMAP-cf7p.10 (SSE Last-Event-ID) and JMAP-cf7p.9 (signal-driven push); these three could land as a coordinated cluster': YES, exactly that landed. .9 was committed in c6c2c21 (signal-driven push); .10+.12 in 127eaf0 (shared replay log).

Wire-format note on pushState encoding: chosen as decimal u64 over alternatives (opaque base64, hex, etc.). Rationale: simplest representation that survives JSON.stringify roundtrip and parses back identically; the encoding is testjig-internal and free to evolve as long as emit-side and parse-side stay in sync. A production push server would likely encode as opaque-bytes to discourage clients from doing arithmetic on the token.

Pre-commit gate clean: cargo fmt, cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace (2125 passed / 0 failed), RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps (no warnings), cargo tree -i openssl --workspace (empty).

This pair (cf7p.10 + .12) closes the last of the three coordinated push beads (.9, .10, .12). The bd:JMAP-cf7p parent epic remains closed (its acceptance was the MVP-stage 8 slices); the 3 follow-up beads are now all closed.
description:
RFC 8887 §4.3.5.2 says:

> The last 'pushState' token that the client received from the server. Upon receipt of a 'pushState' token, the server SHOULD immediately send all changes since that state token.

The bd:JMAP-cf7p.5 WS endpoint parses the pushState field on WebSocketPushEnable but does NOT honor it — clients that reconnect after a missed change must issue Foo/changes themselves. The MVP additionally omits the pushState field from outgoing StateChange frames (RFC 8887 §4.3.5.1 allows omission; clients fall back to /changes).

Same shape as JMAP-cf7p.10 (Last-Event-ID for SSE) — both are spec SHOULDs, not MUSTs, and the right design touches the per-extension MemoryBackend's change-log surface.

Acceptance:
- Outbound StateChange frames include a pushState field per RFC 8887 §4.3.5.1.
- The pushState encodes enough server state that on PushEnable with a prior pushState, the server can emit all StateChange events that have happened since.
- New tests/ws_resume.rs integration test exercises reconnect-with-pushState replay.
- Design likely couples to JMAP-cf7p.10 (SSE Last-Event-ID) and JMAP-cf7p.9 (signal-driven push); these three could land as a coordinated cluster.
title: testjig WS: honor pushState on WebSocketPushEnable per RFC 8887 §4.3.5.2
